title: fr.linagora.twalk.connection.status.changed.v1
description: A connection changed state (ADR 0033, #274): the collector holding an OIDC grant for a mailbox or a calendar says whether it can reach the service, whether the grant still stands, and — when it cannot act — what the operator does next. Produced by the collector that holds the connection; a bridge's state is `bridge.status.changed.v1`, produced by the Companion Gateway, and the two are not merged because a bridge is a transport the Gateway supervises while a collector is the account itself. An operational event: it names nobody and carries no `consent` extension, so a persona is never woken by it (the SDK's trigger allowlist) and its subject is the connection, not a person.

id.description: Deterministic identifier computed as sha256(connection + ':' + to_state + ':' + occurred_at). Re-emitting the same recorded transition produces the same id, and the bus deduplicates on it.

source.description: URI of the connection on the collector that holds it: collector://<host>/connections/<connection id>. The host is the collector's own name in the deployment (COLLECTOR_HOST), never a secret.

type.description: CloudEvents type. Reverse-DNS convention with an explicit version suffix. Any breaking change to this schema requires incrementing the suffix (v2, v3, ...) rather than mutating v1.

time.description: When the event was produced (RFC 3339, UTC).

subject.description: The connection whose state changed. Mirrors data.connection: a consumer filtering on the subject needs no data.

dataschema.description: Optional URI pointing back to this JSON Schema.

traceparent.description: Optional W3C Trace Context traceparent header.

connection.description: Twalk extension (ADR 0033). The connection this event is about, duplicated from data.connection as a NATS header for server-side filtering, like every message-flow type carries it.
The connection, by the id the Companion Gateway's registry gave it (`GET /api/connections`). A collector refuses to start on an id the registry does not know.

kind.description: The connection's kind: `email`, `calendar`. Not the `network` extension, which a calendar is not a value of.

from_state.description: The state before the transition. `unknown` on the first publication of a run: what came before is not this process's to remember, and a consumer reads the first event of a run as the state, not as a change.

to_state.description: The state after the transition. `connected`: the grant renews and every service answers with it. `unreachable`: a service or the SSO did not answer; nothing is wrong with the grant, and the collector retries on its own. `reconnect_required`: the SSO refused to renew the grant (400/401 on refresh) — revoked, expired, or rotated away — and only the operator can give a new one (`twalk-collector consent --renew`). `pending_operator`: a fresh token was refused by a service (401/403) — the grant stands but lacks what that service expects, an audience or a scope — and the operator has to change the client, not the grant. Two refusals, never one: the operator does different things about them.

occurred_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the transition was observed. Part of the id natural key.

service.description: Which service the transition is about, when one is: the SSO for `reconnect_required`, the service that refused a fresh token for `pending_operator`, the one that did not answer for `unreachable`. Absent on `connected`.

hint.description: What the operator does next, in one sentence, for every state but `connected` — the log line's words, on the bus, so a dashboard can show them without reading the log. Never a token, never a URL with a code in it.
